title: Gym Google Ads Settings: Reach Locals, Not Day-Pass Visitors

facts.fact: Keyword Planner shows about 6,600 searches a month nationwide for 'gyms in austin tx' in the page's example market.
facts.quote: In our example market, Austin, Keyword Planner shows about 6,600 searches a month nationwide for "gyms in austin tx."

facts.fact: Of the roughly 6,600 monthly nationwide searches for 'gyms in austin tx,' only about 2,900 come from inside the Austin market itself.
facts.quote: Only about 2,900 of those come from inside the Austin market itself.

facts.fact: The search 'planet fitness austin' gets about 1,900 searches a month nationally and about 1,000 locally, per the page's Keyword Planner figures.
facts.quote: "planet fitness austin" gets about 1,900 a month nationally and about 1,000 locally.

facts.fact: The search 'gym day pass' gets about 8,100 searches a month across the US.
facts.quote: "Gym day pass" alone gets about 8,100 searches a month across the US.

facts.fact: In 2017, location-data firm Dstillery measured gym member travel distance, and the average member who actually went traveled about 4 miles.
facts.quote: The average member who actually went traveled about 4 miles.

facts.fact: In the Dstillery measurement, Blink Fitness members averaged 2.8 miles of travel, Planet Fitness 3.2 miles, SoulCycle 5.5 miles, Equinox 5.7 miles, and The Barre Code 6 miles.
facts.quote: 2.8 miles for Blink Fitness, a low-price chain; 3.2 for Planet Fitness; 5.5 for SoulCycle; 5.7 for Equinox; and 6 for The Barre Code

facts.fact: In the Dstillery measurement, members who went five or more times a month lived closer (3.7 miles) than those who went about once a month (5.1 miles).
facts.quote: People who went five or more times a month lived closer (3.7 miles) than people who went about once a month (5.1).

facts.fact: Google will not draw a location radius smaller than 1 kilometer.
facts.quote: it won't draw one smaller than 1 kilometer

facts.fact: The page recommends a 3 to 5 mile radius for a budget gym and a 5 to 8 mile radius for a boutique studio as starting points, adjusted for local driving patterns.
facts.quote: A budget gym might start at 3 to 5 miles, and a boutique studio at 5 to 8, adjusted for how people actually drive in your area.

facts.fact: Google Ads' 'Presence or interest' location default reaches people in the target area and people who have shown interest in that area from elsewhere.
facts.quote: Google's default setting reaches two groups: people who are in that area or regularly there, and people who've shown interest in it from somewhere else.

facts.fact: Google's help center says new Search campaigns have AI Max turned on by default.
facts.quote: Google's help center says new Search campaigns have it turned on by default.

facts.fact: New Search campaigns include search partners by default in Google Ads.
facts.quote: New Search campaigns include search partners by default

facts.fact: Google's default ad schedule setting is "All day," and the page recommends leaving it on "All day" at launch.
facts.quote: Leave the ad schedule on "All day" at launch, which is Google's default.

facts.fact: Turning off AI Max also turns off final URL expansion.
facts.quote: Turning off AI Max takes them with it.

facts.fact: According to Google, final URL expansion depends on text customization, so switching off text customization also switches off URL expansion.
facts.quote: If you ever turn it back on, Google notes that final URL expansion depends on text customization, so switching off text customization also switches off URL expansion.

facts.fact: Google's call reporting setting logs calls from ads along with their length.
facts.quote: Call reporting: it logs calls from your ads with their length

facts.fact: Google's auto-tagging stamps each ad visit with an identifier so that conversions can be traced to the keyword that paid for them.
facts.quote: Google stamps each ad visit with an identifier, so a trial booked on the website, or a join entered at the front desk and uploaded later, can be traced to the keyword that paid for it.
